newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty, bill yields up amid rate uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty, bill yields up amid rate uncertainty.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed stronger against the basket of currencies in slow trade ahead of a central bank press conference which dispelled talk of a interest rate rise in the near future, dealers said.
They said zloty trade nearly froze after some initial currency sales sparked by the National Bank of Poland president's comments about a possible rate rise to curb the rapid growth of credit action.
"Uncertainty about a possible base rate rise caused banks to keep short currency positions and to withdraw most bids from the market," said Marcin Kaliszewski from Raiffeisen in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 1.83/1.79 percent below the trading band centre, stronger than Wednesday's close at 1.74/1.69.
It was at 2.8147/57 to the dollar, down from 2.8112/16 on Wednesday and at 1.8370/80 to the mark, up from 1.8420/35.

At the central bank's briefing deputy president Witold Kozinski said nominal rates would not rise in the foreseeable future, but that real rates should increase in line with falling inflation, which the bank sees at year-on-year 19 percent in September against August's 20.5 percent .
Polish treasury yields rose in secondary trade as the market priced-in a possible official rise in interest rates.
But dealers expected yields to return to earlier levels on Friday after today's five to 15 basis point rise.
"T-bill yields should come back to yesterday's levels on Friday after the central bank dismissed the possibility of an interest rate rise," said Andrzej Hirsz of Bank Gdanski SA.
Bond yields also rose on Thursday, with the market focused on attractive 16-percent two-year bonds, but foreign investors remained on the sidelines.
The two-year paper yield rose to intraday highs of 20.1/19.95 percent from yesterday's 19.90/19.75 percent.

One-day rates held above the market's main 14-day reverse repo levels, last at 19.14 percent, as the market remained tight despite the central bank's decision not to stage an open market drainage operation today.
Overnight rates closed at 20.3/20.6 percent, slightly below Wednesday's close at 20.5/20.9 and tomrrow/next at 20.3/20.9 percent, nearly flat from yesterday's 20.5/20.9.
